WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him

"Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon." Jeremiah 44:30
"Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land." Jeremiah 37:7

Ezekiel: Zedekiah rebelled by "sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people", but "Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company make for him in the war". Ezekiel 17:15 Ezekiel 17:17
Ezekiel to "Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lieth in the midst of his rivers, which hath said, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself". Ezekiel 29:3
"I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt" (Ezekiel, in the eleventh year). Ezekiel 30:20–21
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
The Jews in Egypt told Jeremiah they would go on burning incense "unto the queen of heaven"; the sign of Hophra was the LORD's answer. Jeremiah 44:15–17 Jeremiah 44:29–30
Zedekiah looked to Egypt for "horses and much people". Ezekiel 17:15
Ezekiel calls Egypt "a staff of reed to the house of Israel". Ezekiel 29:6
Jews settled "at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros". Jeremiah 44:1

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No regnal years. Scripture's nearest dates are Ezekiel's, counted from Jehoiachin's captivity: oracles against Pharaoh in the tenth, eleventh and twelfth years (Ezek 29:1; 30:20; 31:1; 32:1).

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not tell how Jeremiah 44:30 was fulfilled.
Scripture does not name the Pharaoh whose army came out during the siege (Jer 37:5), or say whether it fought the Chaldeans.
Ezekiel never names the Pharaoh of his oracles.
Scripture foretells, but does not narrate, Nebuchadrezzar's attack on Egypt (Jer 43:10–13; Ezek 29:19).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
Scholars' viewPharaoh-hophra is identified with Apries, as Herodotus calls him, the Wahibre of the monuments. Jeremiah 44:30 [16][7][21]

Scholars' viewScripture names Hophra only at Jeremiah 44:30. The person record gathers to him the unnamed "Pharaoh" of Jeremiah 37, 43 and 47 and of Ezekiel 17 and 29–32. Commentators identify Ezekiel's Pharaoh with Hophra (Poole; Gill), and the Pharaoh whose army came out during the siege with him too (Rogers 1912; Nicol 1915; Ellicott's commentary). Jeremiah 37:5 Ezekiel 29:2 [62][63][27][16][56]
